title: Sell Mineral Rights in Faulkner County, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Faulkner County, AR | Fayetteville Shale
metaDescription: Own oil, gas, or mineral rights in Faulkner County, Arkansas? We evaluate core Fayetteville Shale legacy interests countywide and make a straightforward cash offer.
heroLead: Faulkner County, led by Conway, sits at the structural core of the Fayetteville Shale play, one of the most heavily drilled counties in the entire trend.
intro: Between roughly 2005 and 2012, Southwestern Energy and a handful of other operators drilled through Faulkner County about as densely as anywhere in the Fayetteville Shale, and the results generally matched the effort: this was, and remains, one of the strongest-performing counties in the play. That history means Faulkner County mineral owners are more likely than owners almost anywhere else in the state to hold an interest tied to a well with real, substantial production behind it, even though most of those wells are now more than a decade past their peak.

The county has also grown fast. Conway, home to the University of Central Arkansas and Hendrix College, has expanded steadily, and towns like Greenbrier have grown right alongside it. That growth has put mineral ownership questions in front of families who might otherwise never have thought about what's under land that's since been developed, sold, or subdivided.

sections.heading: The most heavily drilled part of the Fayetteville Shale
paragraphs: Faulkner County sits inside the thickest, most productive part of the Fayetteville Shale, and well density here during the boom years was among the highest anywhere in the play. Communities throughout the county, from Conway itself out to Enola, Greenbrier, and Guy, saw substantial leasing and drilling activity, and a large share of that leasehold was actually developed rather than left dormant, unlike some of the play's fringe counties.

That doesn't mean every Faulkner County interest is currently generating strong income. Fayetteville Shale wells decline steeply after their first few years, and even the county's best original wells are now producing at a small fraction of their initial rate. We price interests off current, decline-adjusted production, not the well's historical peak during the boom.

sections.heading: Urban growth, mineral severance, and confirming what you actually own
paragraphs: As Conway and Greenbrier have grown, some land that once held straightforward rural mineral interests has been subdivided for housing or sold multiple times for commercial development. The mineral estate doesn't automatically transfer the same way the surface does in those transactions, meaning some owners assume they still hold minerals under land their family sold years ago when they actually don't, and others assume they lost mineral rights that were in fact reserved and still belong to them.

We check the specific deed chain for a Faulkner County tract as a standard part of any evaluation, since confirming the interest is actually there, and actually belongs to the person we're talking to, has to come before any conversation about price.

sections.heading: Operator history: Southwestern Energy, Flywheel Energy, and BKV Corporation
paragraphs: Southwestern Energy, through its SEECO subsidiary, drilled most of the original Fayetteville Shale wells across Faulkner County. Southwestern sold that entire Fayetteville Shale position to Flywheel Energy, backed by Kayne Anderson, in 2018, and BKV Corporation acquired Flywheel's Fayetteville Shale assets in 2021. If your family's royalty statements have shown more than one operator name over the years, this sequence of transactions is almost certainly why.

We verify current operator and production status directly with the state rather than relying on whatever name last appeared on a statement, since it's common for owners to have outdated information about who's actually running a given well today.

sections.heading: Faulkner County Circuit Clerk records and reconstructing family ownership
paragraphs: The Circuit Clerk's office in Conway holds the county's recorded deeds, oil and gas leases, probate filings, and division orders. Given how many Faulkner County mineral interests have passed through multiple generations, often without a formal partition, and how much surface land has changed hands as the county has grown, reconstructing an accurate ownership picture is frequently more involved here than in more rural, less-developed counties.

We do that reconstruction as part of the offer process, working from whatever an owner has, a deed, a division order, an old lease, or a probate reference, and cross-checking against the Circuit Clerk's index and current operator filings before quoting a number.

faqs.question: Is Faulkner County part of the productive core of the Fayetteville Shale?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's one of the most heavily and successfully drilled counties in the entire play, with well density and results generally among the strongest anywhere in the Fayetteville Shale.

faqs.question: Our family's land near Conway or Greenbrier has been developed or sold since the mineral rights were established. Do we still own them?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but it depends on how the mineral estate was handled in the subsequent sales or subdivision deeds. We check your specific chain of title to confirm before making an offer.

faqs.question: Why does the operator name on our royalty statement keep changing?
faqs.answer: Southwestern Energy's original Fayetteville Shale position moved to Flywheel Energy in 2018 and then to BKV Corporation in 2021. A name change on your statement over the years reflects one of those transactions.

faqs.question: How much has a typical Faulkner County well declined from its original production?
faqs.answer: Substantially. Fayetteville Shale wells lose most of their output within the first few years and now sit on a long, low-volume decline tail, which is where most legacy Faulkner County wells are today. We price based on current output, not historical peak.

faqs.question: Several relatives inherited a share of the same Faulkner County interest. Can you still buy it?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can confirm each person's exact fractional share through Faulkner County Circuit Clerk records in Conway and purchase individual shares without requiring every heir to sell at the same time.
